title: Buehler · Different kinds of departure
description: Separate rankings for 18 selected Markus J. Buehler papers across eras, compared with three strong modern materials-research exemplars. Distinguish conceptual surprise, tested explanatory insight, formal structure and downstream validation.
scope: User-selected key papers across eras. This is a curated 18-paper comparison, not a complete bibliography or a statistically representative sample of materials science.
limitations: Scores are editorial AI judgments on pinned versions, with evidence locators and confidence, not measured novelty, calibrated expert ratings or author prestige.
Four domain readers, one methods auditor and the coordinator share one inherited model family. Role separation does not establish independent model errors.
Axes are conceptually separable but correlated. The Spearman table diagnoses overlap descriptively; it does not prove statistical independence.
CGCNN, NequIP and corrected A-Lab are purposively selected strong comparators, not a statistical sample of conventional papers. Their ranges are illustrative.
A low departure category can accompany strong science. Theory can be rigorous without fabrication; the closure axis records evidence type rather than total rigor.
Ranks cover the full 18-paper corpus and retain ties; filters change visibility, never the reference population. Missing evidence is unranked, not zero.
Categorical prototyping is abstract-only, with five unknown dimensions and low-confidence supported ratings. FieldPerceiver is a partial main-text assessment with unknown robustness.
COPRESHEAF explanation has explicit reviewer disagreement: final 3, low confidence; auditor 2. Its schema-relative symbolic novelty does not establish unique causal mechanics.
No proposed experiment, raw-data reanalysis, code reproduction or independent scientific replication was performed. The webpage shows a recorded assessment; it makes no new AI calls.

papers.title: Nature designs tough collagen: Explaining the nanostructure of collagen fibrils
papers.summary: Two competing critical lengths connect molecular adhesion, slip pulses and rupture to fibril strength and dissipation. The main fibril calculations use a two-dimensional, hydrated, cross-link-free reference. Consequently, the explanatory gain is a mechanism map under explicit assumptions, not a comprehensive reconstruction of living tissue. The measured natural molecular length provides external consistency rather than a new experimental test.

representation.rationale: Critical-length ratios organize mechanisms across molecular and fibril scales.
representation.locator: Results: Critical Molecular Length Scales; Figure 5

transfer.rationale: Griffith-style fracture reasoning transfers within mechanics, rather than between distant domains.

formal.rationale: Analytical scaling laws provide no central formal composition constraint.

dynamics.rationale: Loading-induced slip propagation and rupture are central analyzed responses.

organization.rationale: The scientist specifies the multiscale analysis and parameter sweeps.

explanation.rationale: Competing slip and rupture scales discriminate failure mechanisms.

validation.rationale: Atomistically parameterized mesoscopic simulations test predictions; no new fabrication.

robustness.rationale: Lengths, adhesion, cross-links and geometries vary; physiological alternatives remain open.
robustness.locator: Results: Bimolecular Assemblies; Larger Collagen Fibrils

surprise.observation: Stronger adhesion can eventually favor brittle molecular rupture.
surprise.interpretation: Maximizing bond strength alone need not maximize toughness.
surprise.boundary: Model mechanics do not establish evolutionary optimization.

detail.observation: The slip threshold shifts from roughly 42 nm in pairs to 200 nm in fibrils.
detail.consequence: Boundary conditions and confinement change the inferred design scale.

notRead: Supporting information; underlying atomistic trajectories

papers.title: Nanoconfinement controls stiffness, strength and mechanical toughness of β-sheet crystals in silk
papers.version: Nature Materials 9, 359–367; published online March 14, 2010; author-hosted advance publication PDF
papers.summary: Nanoconfinement makes weak hydrogen bonds cooperate through uniform shear and repeated bond reformation. The comparison tests pure bending against combined shear and bending, making the added mechanism consequential. Critical strand length also bounds how far crystal dimensions can grow. Cited experimental shear moduli were not measured on individual silk nanocrystals, limiting the directness of validation.

representation.rationale: Crystal size and strain distribution explain collective bond performance.

transfer.rationale: Continuum shear–bending theory interprets molecular deformation within mechanics.

formal.rationale: No central formal composition or transport constraint drives this mechanics contribution.

dynamics.rationale: Bending, pull-out and stick–slip trajectories are central analyzed responses.

organization.rationale: Fixed computational experiments do not reorganize a discovery workflow.

explanation.rationale: Strain localization and cooperative rupture distinguish small from large crystals.

validation.rationale: Molecular dynamics and DFT support mechanics; experiments are external comparisons.

robustness.rationale: Alternative beam models, size sweeps and pulling rates discriminate mechanisms.
robustness.locator: Figure 3; Methods: Application of boundary conditions

surprise.observation: Smaller crystals can simultaneously improve stiffness, strength and dissipation.
surprise.interpretation: Weak-bond architecture can overcome constituent weakness.
surprise.boundary: Nanocrystal behavior is not a complete model of whole silk.

detail.observation: Experimental-rate pull-out forces require an estimated sixfold reduction; the transition length survives rate variation.
detail.consequence: The robust claim concerns the mechanism and length scale, rather than raw simulated force.

rubric.scale: Eight separate ordinal axes, 0–4; null means insufficient reviewed evidence. Rank separately on each axis, keep ties, and assign no total score. A low departure score is not poor science.

anchors: One domain; no transfer central to contribution
Analogy or familiar technique transfer
Operational mapping between related domains
Explicit mapping between distant domains
Distant-domain mapping with consequential instantiated tests

axes.label: Formal composition and guarantees
axes.question: Does formal structure constrain which transformations and compositions are valid?
anchors: No such formal constraint central
Structured notation or interfaces
Formal constraints on a limited component
Explicit compositional conditions or checked invariants
Nontrivial composition or transport guarantee instantiated and checked

axes.label: Dynamics as a design target
axes.question: Is motion, response or adaptation itself designed or explained, rather than only a static property?
anchors: Static property or representation
Dynamic data used mainly for static endpoints
Dynamic response analyzed as a central outcome
Response behavior or dynamical function explicitly targeted
Inverse design or composition directly targets detailed temporal or modal behavior

axes.label: Discovery-process self-organization
axes.question: Can the discovery process change its division of work or coordination through artifacts and needs?
anchors: Single fixed analysis or predictor
Automated fixed pipeline
Specialized agents with prescribed coordination
Artifact- or need-driven distributed coordination
Executed revision of workflow or coordination with explicit gates

axes.label: Mechanistic explanatory gain
axes.question: Does the work expose a concise, discriminating mechanism or relation beyond producing candidates or predictions?
anchors: No mechanistic explanation assessed
Plausible narrative or generated hypothesis
Quantified interpretable relationship
Mechanism distinguishes alternatives with scoped tests
Strongly tested non-obvious relation with converging evidence

axes.label: Validation closure
axes.question: How far do the actual results close the loop from proposal to downstream evidence?
anchors: No executed downstream check reviewed
Examples or model-generated evaluation
Executable benchmark or surrogate calculation
Direct physics simulation or model-system implementation
Physical fabrication, synthesis or experiment tests the central contribution

axes.label: Counterfactual and robustness support
axes.question: Do ablations, alternative explanations, held-out tests and uncertainty distinguish why the method or insight works?
anchors: No relevant comparison reviewed
Illustrative or narrow comparison
Relevant baselines with important alternatives open
Multiple discriminating controls or held-out sensitivity checks
Extensive independent or converging tests of central alternatives

protocol: Read methods/results, pin versions and declare coverage. Unknown evidence is null, not a zero or a proven omission.
Record one unexpected contribution and one consequential detail missed by abstract-only reading; separate observation from interpretation.
Category-theoretic consistency is conditional on correct models and interfaces, not a guarantee of empirical truth.
Simulation and experimental validation are distinct. Generated hypotheses and agent scores do not establish material properties.
Use three explicit modern materials-research comparators rather than claim to measure all conventional materials science. A-Lab is a strong autonomy comparator, not an ordinary low-capability foil.
Report within-corpus competition ranks with ties. Compare ordinal categories directly to comparator ranges; never sum departure dimensions into prestige or quality.
Surprise may mean a reader's conceptual update, changed representation, or a tested mechanistic finding. These are different claims.
Audit axes for overlap and evidence calibration. All reader and auditor contexts inherit one model family; role separation does not establish independent errors.
